subject: Strange deadlock with transaction lock targets
symptom: Concurrent work deadlocks on transaction ID locks even though the application does not explicitly lock tables.

subject: Fix self-deadlock during DROP SUBSCRIPTION
symptom: DROP SUBSCRIPTION can self-deadlock when a same-server publisher connection needs pg_subscription while the command holds a conflicting lock.

subject: Latches versus lightweight-lock contention
symptom: A lock-timeout cleanup path can revisit an already released awaited lock and crash the server under concurrent DDL and COPY activity.

subject: Long-running dry-run transaction without blocking
symptom: A validation workload keeps a transaction open for hours and interferes with concurrent application activity despite eventually rolling back.

subject: Could not access status of transaction
symptom: LISTEN can access a transaction status already removed after vacuum advances frozen horizons while an async notification entry remains.

subject: Aggressive vacuum
symptom: A large table triggers disruptive aggressive freezing despite table-level autovacuum threshold and freeze-age tuning.

subject: High CPU on selects during vacuum
symptom: Select workloads become CPU-bound near the end of a large table vacuum heap scan while millions of tuples are frozen.

subject: Repeated pg_commit_ts truncation and autovacuum restarts
symptom: Repeated commit-timestamp truncation attempts coincide with restarting autovacuum workers and severe replica lag on an Aurora PostgreSQL deployment.

subject: Fix per-relation memory leakage in autovacuum
symptom: An autovacuum worker leaks per-relation statistics and option structures until its run ends, particularly affecting databases with many relations.

subject: Autovacuum scheduling and wraparound priority
symptom: Default relation ordering can vacuum lower-risk tables before one near the failsafe transaction age, delaying urgent anti-wraparound work.

subject: B-tree page merge during vacuum
symptom: A proposed vacuum-time B-tree page merge intended to reduce index bloat may duplicate or skip scan results without stronger concurrency handling.

subject: Parallel index-level reindexdb behavior
symptom: Index-level reindexdb with multiple jobs fails to use the expected parallelism because indexes for each relation are scheduled serially.

subject: Fix index-level REINDEX with multiple jobs
symptom: A second asynchronous REINDEX command on one connection waits for the first, defeating index-level parallel execution until commands are grouped per table.
